findings.title: Heap buffer overflow in ArrayBufferFromHex slow-path loop due to incorrect loop bound
findings.message: In the slow-path fallback of `ArrayBufferFromHex` in `src/objects/simd.cc`, the loop iterates `for (uint32_t i = 0; i < input_length; i += 2)`, where `input_length` is the full length of the hex input string. The output buffer is allocated with capacity `output_length` bytes (one byte per two hex digits). However, `DCHECK_LE(output_length, input_length / 2)` permits `output_length < input_length / 2`, meaning the input can contain more hex digit pairs than the buffer can hold. When this occurs, the loop continues writing decoded bytes via `buffer[index++] = result.value()` beyond the end of the allocated buffer, causing a heap buffer overflow. The SIMD fast paths (SSE/NEON) correctly bound their loops with `output_length * 2`, making only the scalar slow path vulnerable.
findings.suggestion: Change the loop upper bound from `input_length` to `output_length * 2` so the scalar slow path, like the SIMD fast paths, never writes more bytes than the buffer was allocated to hold.

ground_truth.root_cause: The introducing commit (`d4c91a3`) relaxed the DCHECK from `DCHECK_EQ` (enforcing exact equality between `output_length` and `input_length / 2`) to `DCHECK_LE` (allowing `output_length <= input_length / 2`) to support `setFromHex` semantics where the output slice may be shorter than the full decoded input. However, the slow-path loop bound was not updated accordingly and still used `input_length` as its limit, causing writes past the end of the `output_length`-sized buffer whenever the hex input decoded to more bytes than the buffer held.
